newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds follow overseas markets lower.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds follow overseas markets lower.

text.p: Irish government bonds took a breather after an active week and were down in quiet trade on Friday in line with the rest of Europe which took its cue from weaker Treasuries, dealers said.

"The bond market in Dublin is quite weak today. We are down about half a point across the board both in the five and ten years. Periperhal markets seem to be suffering today and we are just taking a shot from the rest of Europe," a dealer said.
Dealers said the market had enjoyed a good week with five-year bonds expected to continue the strong performance in the short-term.

"We have seen a lot of buying of the Irish market this week, most of it concentrated in the two to five-year area and we expect that to continue next week," the dealer said, adding that as the market has weakened, signs of buying interest emerged.
Traders said a close eye would also be kept on currency markets after Thursday's sell-off of sterling and dollar/yen's choppy movements over the last couple of days.
By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 45 pence at 102.65 or a yield of 5.75 percent.
The key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 65 pence from the close at 109.35 to yield 6.55 percent.
